solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Official in struggle for small plant

indicators.note: one word sits in another, so the first is placed inside the second

blocks.note: to toil is to struggle or labour
a ref, short for referee, is a match official

explanation.surface: A referee caught up in a hard struggle, apparently on behalf of a tiny plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefoil is clover or a similar low herb with three-part leaves, a small plant.

clue.text: Loony mate ignoring tips at work — he's associated with many a vice

definitions.text: he's associated with many a vice

indicators.note: tips are the ends of the words, and ignoring them means dropping each final letter
letters at work are busily moving about, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the word with its last letter dropped
the word with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A crazy partner at work is linked with plenty of wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'vice' is not wickedness but the workshop clamp: a TOOLMAN works at a bench with a vice.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolman is a worker with tools, and a bench vice is a standard piece of his equipment, hence the cryptic description.

clue.text: Run one, or two if start's recalled

indicators.note: the start is called back and withdrawn, so the first letter is removed

blocks.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds

explanation.surface: A starter recalls a false start, turning one run into two.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue also reads as R (run, in cricket) plus ACE (one), so 'Run one' gives the answer directly as well as defining it; a brace losing its first letter is the second route.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a race, or a race itself, is a single run against others, a contest of speed.

clue.text: Weaver from Portuguese resort cheated, nothing less

indicators.note: less means without, so the zero is taken away from the resort name

blocks.note: Estoril is a seaside resort near Lisbon
nothing is zero, the letter O
to do someone is to cheat them

explanation.surface: Someone from a Portuguese holiday town got swindled and ended up with nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrildids are the waxbills and their kin, small finches known as weaver-finches, so weaver is a bird name here.

clue.text: Thoroughly upset stuff in contest?

blocks.note: as in out-and-out, completely
to eat someone is to trouble them, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly upset over food at a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: to outeat a rival is to stuff yourself harder in an eating contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To outeat is to eat more than another person, which is exactly winning a contest of stuffing oneself.

clue.text: Heraldic beasts painted in cellulose, not for all to see

indicators.note: not tells us a letter is to be left out of the material
something painted is made over into a new picture, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Coats of arms painted in cellulose paint, kept from public view.
explanation.walkthrough: U is removed from cellulose; the remaining letters plus IN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lioncelles are small lions in heraldry, used when several appear on one shield, so they are heraldic beasts.

clue.text: Having no direction, senior nurses caught sadly short

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so a final letter goes
to nurse is to hold close, so the senior abbreviation holds the rest

blocks.note: Sr is the standard abbreviation for senior
c is caught in cricket scoring
alas is a cry of sorrow; shortened by its last letter

explanation.surface: An elderly man nursing someone caught short, in a rather aimless way.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a scalar quantity has magnitude only, unlike a vector, which also has direction.

clue.text: Ace bowler perhaps brought back for South African flier

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so read it in reverse

blocks.note: A is ace on playing cards
a bowler is a kind of hat, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A star bowler recalled to the side for a South African pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' wants to be cricket; it is the hard round hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The taha is a South African weaver bird, so it is a flier native to that country.

clue.text: Expression heard for body of soldiers years ago

indicators.note: heard tells us to go by how a word sounds when spoken

blocks.note: a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: An old phrase overheard about a troop from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Turm is an obsolete word for a troop, especially of horsemen, so a body of soldiers in archaic use.

clue.text: Have teg finally, thanks to a shepherd's club

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of the preceding word only

blocks.note: ha' is an old dialect form of have
a teg is a sheep in its second year; only its final letter is used
ta is informal British for thanks
per means for each, a, as in a pound a head

explanation.surface: A farmer finally gets a young sheep, thanks to a shepherd's stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shepherd's club' looks like a crook; it is a plant name, and the sheep-farming surface hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: Hag-taper is an old name for great mullein, also called shepherd's club, a tall woolly plant.

clue.text: One old coin associated with a quarter

blocks.note: a means one
the real was an old Spanish silver coin

explanation.surface: A single antique coin linked with a quarter, like a twenty-five-cent piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Areal means relating to an area, and a quarter is a district or area of a town.

clue.text: Railway special involving diversion for some

indicators.note: involving says the new material is brought into the longer word
for means in place of, so one piece swaps out the other

blocks.note: particular means special or specific
fun is amusement, a diversion
some of something is part of it

explanation.surface: A special train service that involves a detour for some passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diversion' reads as a rerouting of trains; it is amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: A funicular is a cable-hauled railway up a steep slope, with cars balancing each other.

clue.text: One month to get a measure of Sky

blocks.note: Oct is the calendar abbreviation for October
a means one

explanation.surface: One month's subscription to a television service called Sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite TV company, which the capital invites; here it is the actual sky.
explanation.definitionFit: An octa (okta) is one eighth of the sky, the unit meteorologists use to measure cloud cover.

clue.text: Minor motoring brushes can lead to combustible cases

blocks.note: the Morris Minor was a popular British car
a brush is a light touch

explanation.surface: Small scrapes on the road can end in lawsuits that blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' suggests court cases following minor collisions; they are cartridge cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche was a paper case holding a gun's powder charge, so such cases burn readily.

clue.text: Rowing movement ending in hullabaloo and absolute fury

indicators.note: ending in points at the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: its final letter
A is the abbreviation for absolute, as in temperature scales
rage is fury

explanation.surface: A rowing stroke ends in uproar and pure fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarage is an archaic word for the use or motion of oars, so a rowing action.

clue.text: Eagle seen in ground briefly on a swamp

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped
something seen in a place sits inside it

blocks.note: land is ground; shortened by one letter
the erne is the sea eagle

explanation.surface: A sea eagle spotted landing briefly on marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lernean means of Lerna, the marsh where Heracles killed the Hydra, so it describes something on that swamp.

clue.text: Party member overseeing golf tournament made public

indicators.note: in a down entry, overseeing places the first piece directly above the second

blocks.note: someone in is a member of the governing party
The Open is golf's oldest major championship

explanation.surface: A politician supervises a golf championship and the news goes public.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the open is no longer secret, the idiom for being revealed to everyone.

clue.text: Scottish lover long forgotten by Indian head

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so a letter is dropped from the following word

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for long
a malik is a headman or chief in India

explanation.surface: A Highland sweetheart long forgotten by an Indian chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Maik is a Scots word for a mate or match, a partner and so a lover.

clue.text: Wilde's bachelor, large libertine with no end of invention

indicators.note: a libertine is unrestrained and loose, so these letters are let loose into a new order
end of points at the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
its final letter

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde's single man, a big rake lacking any imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon Moncrieff is the idle bachelor in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest.

clue.text: Girl, 50 gets entry for a year

blocks.note: a girl's name
L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A girl of fifty gets admitted for twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: Annals are yearly records, so a single annal is the record entered for one year.

clue.text: Will's share is a large draw

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a lottery is a draw of tickets

explanation.surface: An inheritance under a will turns out to be a big prize draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a legal testament; it is William Shakespeare, who uses this word in As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Allottery is Shakespeare's word for an allotted portion, so a share in his usage.

clue.text: Lorna Doone novel one's left in US city

indicators.note: one has left means that word has departed from the title
novel means new, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: the title of Blackmore's romance, taken as written

explanation.surface: A copy of the novel Lorna Doone left behind in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like it describes Lorna Doone, which is indeed a novel, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a city in central Florida, a US city famous for its theme parks.

clue.text: Boiler has to be put out? Extinguisher needed

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boiler on fire must be put out, so a fire extinguisher is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' and 'Extinguisher' set up a fire scene; the extinguisher is anything that does away with something.
explanation.definitionFit: To extinguish can mean to abolish or wipe out, so one who abolishes is an extinguisher.

clue.text: German vehicle project

blocks.note: first meaning: the Volkswagen small car
second meaning: to jut out or overhang, as beetling brows do

explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' reads as a noun, a scheme for a German car; it is the verb meaning stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: The VW car is nicknamed after the insect, and as a verb the word means to overhang or protrude.

clue.text: Like ancient Greek music, sparkling stuff fills one part of concert

indicators.note: part of the next word means only its opening letter is used
something that fills another goes inside it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
its first letter
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Fizzy wine poured out during part of a concert of ancient Greek music.
explanation.definitionFit: Iastic means Ionian, describing one of the modes of ancient Greek music.

clue.text: Hour with a German poet

blocks.note: h is the abbreviation for hour
eine is German for a

explanation.surface: An hour spent with a German poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinrich Heine was a nineteenth-century German lyric poet, whose verses Schubert and Schumann set.

clue.text: Must stop eating nuts when short of money

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is taken away
something eating another takes it inside

blocks.note: ho is an old call to stop or halt
mast is the fallen nuts of beech and oak
M is the abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: You must stop eating nuts when you are short of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' wants to be a snack or madness; mast is the woodland fruit pigs feed on.
explanation.definitionFit: Has to is the everyday idiom meaning must, being obliged to.

clue.text: Bird in shed is a blackbird

indicators.note: to shed is to cast off, so the word in front is removed from the bird

blocks.note: the merlin is a small falcon
taken as written; this is what is cast off

explanation.surface: The bird in the garden shed is a blackbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' reads as a garden hut; it is the verb meaning drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Merl or merle is an old and Scots name for the blackbird.

clue.text: With weak acting, Director's beginning to try black lead

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word means just its first letter

blocks.note: w is an abbreviation for weak
A is the abbreviation for acting, as in a temporary post
D is the abbreviation for director
its first letter

explanation.surface: Faced with poor acting, the director first tries a darker pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: Wad or wadt is a dialect word for graphite, which is also called black lead or plumbago.

clue.text: What would be misplaced as Germany, east coast? Worms

indicators.note: this asks what word, its letters put in the wrong places, would turn into the words that follow

blocks.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
E is east on a compass
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geography slip: which place could be confused with Germany's eastern shore?
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: the answer is the word whose letters, jumbled, make D, E and COAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Cestoda is the class of tapeworms, parasitic flatworms, so it names a group of worms.

clue.text: Duncan's end: heartlessly cut up

indicators.note: without its heart, the word loses its middle letter
in a down entry, up means the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: diced means cut into cubes

explanation.surface: King Duncan's murder in Macbeth: cut up without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: Duncan is the Scottish king of Macbeth, so the definition calls for Scots: deid is the Scots spelling of dead and death.
explanation.definitionFit: Duncan's end was his death, and deid is the Scots word for death, fitting a Scottish king.

clue.text: Handle ordered from Athens

indicators.note: ordered means put into a different arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A handle ordered by mail from a firm in Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneath or snath is the long curved shaft of a scythe, the handle the mower holds.

clue.text: Magistrate has space for writing device

blocks.note: JP is a Justice of the Peace, a lay magistrate
an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A magistrate keeps room on the desk for a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A J-pen is a broad-nibbed pen once sold for clerical work, a tool for writing.

clue.text: Cheers much reduced parking in the end

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the last letter goes
what comes before sits in what follows

blocks.note: a tip is an end or extremity
oodles means lots, much
P is the road-sign letter for parking

explanation.surface: Car-park charges sharply cut in the end, which deserves a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' reads as a toast or thanks; here it is the British goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-pip is jaunty, dated British slang for goodbye, as cheers can also mean farewell.

clue.text: Beginning short of energy once

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the letter that follows is removed

blocks.note: the onset is the start
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A start made without energy, just the one time.
explanation.definitionFit: Onst is an archaic form of the adverb meaning a single time, used by Spenser.

clue.text: Inferior leader of orchestra getting duet's lower part

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so the opening letter is used

blocks.note: second-rate, inferior
its first letter

explanation.surface: A second-rate leader of an orchestra lands the bottom part of a duet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of orchestra' suggests the first violinist; here it simply means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In a piano duet the secondo is the player or part taking the lower half of the keyboard.
